channel.description: Latest articles from Space.com (Future plc US Inc.) (space.com)

item.title: Can you really survive on Mars? What science fiction gets wrong about off-world living
item.description: Arnie said, "Get your ass to Mars", but is it really a good idea? We asked the experts about our Martian future.

item.title: What's the point of a space station around the moon?
item.description: Is an orbiting space station necessary to achieve lunar objectives, including scientific ones?

item.title: Canon PowerShot V1 review
item.description: I tried out Canon's latest vlogging camera for astrophotography, the PowerShot V1 and managed to capture the Andromeda galaxy and the Milky Way!

item.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 198 — A Dragonfly on Titan
item.description: On Episode 198 of This Week In Space, Rod Pyle and Tariq Malik talk with Principal Investigator Dr. Elizabeth "Zibi" Turtle about the Dragonfly mission and what to expect in the coming years.

item.title: NASA's Artemis 2 moon rocket has a problem and it's leaving the launch pad. Don't expect a moonshot in March
item.description: NASA on Sunday (Sept. 22) announced that the space agency will roll its massive Artemis 2 moon rocket to fix a helium system glitch on the massive booster.

item.title: Falcon 9 rocket sets new reuse record on SpaceX's 2nd Starlink launch of the day (video)
item.description: Two SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets, each carrying Starlink satellites, launched from California and Florida on Saturday, Feb. 21, 2026. The second booster set a new reuse record.

item.title: A risky maneuver could send a spacecraft to interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS. Here's the plan
item.description: By taking advantage of a maneuver that would see a spacecraft fire rocket engines while in the solar corona, that spacecraft’s velocity could receive a huge boost — enough to allow it to catch up with 3I/ATLAS, which is the fastest comet ever seen.

item.title: Why do some places on Earth get far more solar eclipses than others?
item.description: Why do some places wait 1,000 years to see a total solar eclipse while others get two in a decade? The surprising orbital mechanics behind where eclipses happen — and don't.

item.title: NASA's Perseverance rover now has its own 'GPS' on Mars: 'We've given the rover a new ability'
item.description: NASA's Perseverance rover can now pinpoint its exact location on Mars without help from Earth, paving the way for longer, more autonomous exploration.

item.title: Is time a fundamental part of reality? A quiet revolution in physics suggests not
item.description: It feels so obvious that time moves forward that questioning it can seem almost pointless.
